question: Does a controller have enough genuine out-of-fold evidence within one ordinary run to learn how much to trust an additional member? The earlier single-fold routing fits used small slices; this study pools completed earlier training folds, without obtaining any new base-model fit.
arms: Use the first and already registered second, disjoint, ordinary course-training panels on the recruitment runtime. Only a real run that accepted a fractional binary vote, delivered an independently reloaded model, and has an unused training allowance is eligible. Infer member identities and weights from that run's own evidence. Do not substitute a manually chosen member for a refused or unavailable election.
learning: Pool all common row-aligned held probabilities on primary, confirmation_1 and confirmation_2 for which every necessary constituent was actually fitted. Require at least two complete folds, 80 independent disagreement groups and both correctness outcomes. A single penalized logistic correction takes the log ratio of the two weighted absolute class-probability margins as its offset, with a learned intercept and two log-scaled margin terms. Penalize parameters by sqrt(number of disagreements). This changes decisions only on disagreements. Never use outside labels or train the gate on its two later review folds.
checks: Freeze all parameters before the two separate recruitment review folds. Enable the correction only if neither fold loses accuracy to the accepted vote and the combined gain on those two folds reaches +0.20 percentage points. Keep an unmodified deployable vote on insufficient support or a failed check. Freeze both the unrestricted shadow and the accepted predictions for the outer feature packet, verify the protected vote against that run's exact sealed predictions, then open only the corresponding training-development audit labels. Report both the practical and shadow results. Require two eligible panels with a real positive net gain each and +0.20 pooled points before any proposed change to the runtime.
budget: At most one supervised correction per run, zero new base fits or model API calls, and no course designated validation, formal test or H2. These are known development data; the second ordinary run's outcome had not been observed when registering this design.
